newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bulk millfeeds-Prices mostly steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bulk millfeeds-Prices mostly steady to higher.

text.p: U.S. millfeed prices were mostly steady to higher on Tuesday as several dealers reported a mixed picture on nearby demand.
"Dry grass is burning up," a North Texas dealer said, referring to the high temperatures in his region. "Feed business has picked up," he said.

In Chattanooga, one broker said the market had a steady tone. "I think it has something to do with grain prices," he said. Chicago Board of Trade corn futures rose on Tuesday and deferred soymeal values were up.
One Midwest dealer said demand was "mediocre" at best.
"So we will go up slowly with the (CBOT) board ... but we won't go up big time until we see an improvement in feed business," he said.

The Southeast market remained featureless with many using cheaper substitutes like soyhulls in their ingredients Soyhulls are offered at probably $60 delivered, which is $30 cheaper than midds, a North Carolina dealer said.
He added the market was quiet with buyers holding off on the deferreds.
